thesis: Western Digital (now WD) is a leading HDD manufacturer and a prime beneficiary of the AI data center storage buildout following its February 2026 separation from SanDisk (NAND flash). FY2026 revenue rose 36% to $12.9B with gross margin expanding to 49.1% and EPS more than doubling to $10.22. Q4 FY2026 delivered $3.75B revenue (+44% YoY) with non-GAAP gross margin of 54.4% and free cash flow of $1.3B. The company is the pure-play HDD leader as AI data lakes and cloud nearline storage demand surge. At ~31x P/E the stock is fairly valued for a cyclical that is now in a structural up-cycle, but capacity-driven pricing power and AI demand visibility support a BUY rating.

drivers: AI data lake and cloud nearline HDD demand drives multi-year volume and pricing upcycle
Capacity HDD technology leadership (HAMR/ePMR) sustains premium margins
Post-SanDisk separation refocuses capital allocation and simplifies the equity story
FY2027 revenue and margin expansion as AI infrastructure buildout accelerates

base_case.assumptions: FY2027 revenue grows 15–20% as nearline HDD demand stays strong, gross margins hold near 50%, and EPS reaches $12–14. Market applies a 35–40x multiple on moderate cyclical growth, keeping the stock near current levels.

risks: HDD demand cyclicality reasserts as cloud capex normalizes or NAND flash pricing improves
Seagate gains share in nearline HDDs or HAMR technology narrows WDC's lead
AI storage demand shifts more toward SSD/flash at the expense of HDD
Macro-driven enterprise IT spending slowdown compresses multiples

catalysts.event: Q4 FY2026 earnings reported — revenue $3.75B (+44% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $3.56, gross margin 54.4%
Q1 FY2027 earnings — demand visibility and pricing trends for nearline HDDs
Next-gen HAMR and ePMR capacity HDD ramps for hyperscaler data centers

key_risks: HDD is inherently cyclical; a demand downturn could compress margins sharply
Post-separation, WDC is a single-segment company with limited product diversification
Competition from Seagate in nearline HDDs and from SSDs in enterprise storage
Macro or cloud capex deceleration could slow AI data lake spending
Stock has rallied significantly from 52-week lows (~$73), limiting near-term upside potential
